title: Have one coding agent plan and another build the code
summary: A developer built a relay where Codex plans and reviews while Claude Code writes code, pausing for human decisions; one live run is reported as verified.
agent_role: Codex writes the plan and reviews, Claude Code implements, and the relay passes turns between them; the human answers questions and sets turn and time limits.
outcome: The README reports a verified live run where Codex led Claude Code.
what_they_did: The developer built a tool that hands each turn between a Codex session and a Claude Code session. It records every step on disk and stops when a decision is needed. A web console shows progress, even on a phone.
how_it_went: The author reports Codex led Claude Code in a live test. Other features are built but not yet verified live.
worth_knowing: The relay cannot see what an agent does inside a turn, so one turn can hide a lot of work. A per-turn time limit is the only hard cap.
prompt: Act as the planner and reviewer for [task] in [repo]. Write a short plan, hand the coding to a second agent, then review its changes. Repeat for at most [number] rounds. Stop and ask me whenever a decision is needed, and do not merge or deploy anything without my approval.

curation.rationale: Early prototype that passes work between Codex and Claude Code with human stops; code and a live verified run exist, but no concrete task outcome is reported.
